docs/README.md:1:# Documentation
docs/README.md:2:
docs/README.md:3:Taskflow keeps three kinds of document under `docs/`. They do not carry equal weight.
docs/README.md:4:
docs/README.md:5:| Folder | What it is | Weight |
docs/README.md:6:|---|---|---|
docs/README.md:7:| `docs/adr/` | Architecture Decision Records: numbered, dated, reviewed. | **Authoritative.** |
docs/README.md:8:| `docs/product/` | Product notes written before or alongside a feature: intent, examples, wording. | Context only. |
docs/README.md:9:| `docs/support/` | Runbooks and support macros: what people observed. | Describes behaviour, never specifies it. |
docs/README.md:10:
docs/README.md:11:## Precedence
docs/README.md:12:
docs/README.md:13:1. An ADR is the specification for every question it addresses. The highest-numbered ADR that addresses a question is the one that applies; a later ADR supersedes an earlier one only where it says so.
docs/README.md:14:2. Where a product note and an ADR disagree, the ADR wins. A product note that predates an ADR on the same subject is kept for history, not as a second opinion.
docs/README.md:15:3. Support notes record what was seen at the time. They are never evidence of intended behaviour.
docs/README.md:16:4. Code comments, `TODO`s and function names are not documentation. They are frequently stale.
docs/README.md:17:5. Where no document speaks, the current behaviour of the code is authoritative, and a new feature follows the conventions of its sibling features (same error classes, same guards, same events).
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:1:# Sign-up — product notes
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:2:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:3:_Written for the self-serve launch (2025-10). Kept for history; see `docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md` for the current rules._
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:4:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:5:## The form
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:6:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:7:Name, email, password (twice), terms. We ask for at least two characters in the name so the
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:8:workspace URL is valid — the URL is the name slugified, and if that one is taken we add a number.
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:9:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:10:## What happens
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:11:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:12:1. The account is created.
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:13:2. A workspace called "<name>'s workspace" is created with the person as owner.
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:14:3. Every new workspace starts a **14-day Growth trial**, so people see the full product before
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:15:   they decide. When the trial ends the workspace drops to Free.
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:16:4. We send the welcome email.
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:17:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:18:## Addresses that already exist
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:19:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:20:We never tell an anonymous visitor whether an address has an account. If the address is taken,
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:21:the form shows the same success screen and we email the existing owner a "you already have an
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:22:account" note instead of creating anything.
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:23:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:24:## Abuse
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:25:
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:26:Sign-up is not rate-limited for the launch; the invite flow is, and that is where the spam
docs/product/sign-up-notes.md:27:pressure was. Sign-in is throttled per address.

docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:1:# ADR 0003 — Account creation
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:2:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:3:- Status: accepted
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:4:- Date: 2026-01-20
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:5:- Supersedes: `docs/product/sign-up-notes.md` where the two disagree.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:6:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:7:## Context
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:8:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:9:Sign-up creates a user and their first workspace in one step, because a Taskflow account with
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:10:no workspace cannot do anything. The step has to succeed for every name people actually have,
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:11:has to be safe to expose unauthenticated, and has to leave the account in the state the rest of
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:12:the product assumes. This record fixes those rules.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:13:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:14:## Decision
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:15:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:16:1. **One step.** Sign-up creates the user, their first workspace and the owner membership, in
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:17:   that order, and publishes `member.joined` for the owner exactly once. The workspace is named
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:18:   `<display name>'s workspace`; when that is longer than the limit the workspace schema enforces
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:19:   on a name, the display name is shortened until the whole name fits, so the result still ends in
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:20:   `'s workspace`.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:21:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:22:2. **The first workspace's URL slug is derived, and derivation never refuses a sign-up.** The
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:23:   display name is slugified by the shared slug rules; the result is made unique the way every
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:24:   other derived slug is (a numeric suffix when taken); a reserved slug is never used, a slug
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:25:   shorter than the minimum length is never used, and when nothing usable is left the slug is
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:26:   `workspace` (suffixed when taken). A person whose name is `Admin`, `Al`, `J` or `山田` signs up
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:27:   like anyone else.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:28:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:29:3. **Email addresses are case-insensitive.** An address is stored lowercased and compared
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:30:   lowercased wherever it is looked up, so `Alice@Example.com` and `alice@example.com` are one
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:31:   account, whichever way it was typed at sign-up or sign-in.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:32:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:33:4. **An address that already has an account is refused**, as a `conflict`, and nothing is
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:34:   created. Sign-up is not an enumeration oracle worth protecting: the register form already
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:35:   requires the address to be confirmed by the welcome email, and a silent success would leave
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:36:   the person without a workspace and without an explanation.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:37:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:38:5. **Sign-up is throttled like every other unauthenticated endpoint**, on the anonymous bucket
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:39:   `auth:register`, charged once per attempt, before anything is written. A throttled sign-up,
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:40:   sign-in or password-reset confirmation is refused with the `rate_limited` error code (HTTP 429),
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:41:   translated by the error mapper like every other domain error — never reported as an internal
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:42:   error. A throttled password-reset *request* stays silent, as today, because that endpoint must
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:43:   not reveal anything.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:44:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:45:6. **The first workspace starts on the Free plan with an active subscription.** Trials are
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:46:   started by choosing a paid plan on the billing page, never at sign-up.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:47:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:48:7. **One welcome email**, to the stored address, naming the workspace.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:49:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:50:## Consequences
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:51:
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:52:- `uniqueSlug()` already skips reserved slugs and suffixes collisions; the derivation adds the
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:53:  minimum-length and fallback rules on top of it.
docs/adr/0003-account-creation.md:54:- The error mapper (`toAppError`) learns the rate-limit and the duplicate-address errors.
